subject: Novamed production: hosted API p99 spikes on long-window sessions — executive summary
body:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novamed.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production alert: p99 latency spikes on long-window requests

Diego —

We started seeing elevated p99 latency on hosted API requests that use long context windows (16k and 32k) starting around 08:45 PT. Impacting several inference-heavy endpoints; customers using larger system prompts are seeing stalls and occasional 504s. SRE attached a sample trace and QPS histogram.

We believe the spike correlates with a rollout you completed this morning (model variant + kernel change). Can you confirm? Novamed is in active clinical trials; this is high priority.

Attached: novamed_trace_20260911.jsonl, prod_qps_trend_09-11.csv

— Priya Shah
SRE, Novamed
priya.shah@novamed.com

-----Original message appended by diego_fernandez@redwood.ai-----

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: infra-oncall@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Production alert: p99 latency spikes on long-window requests

Thanks for the heads up, Priya — we see the traces and are looking now. I'm escalating to infra and quoting Marcus.

Marcus / Infra on-call: please triage kernel selection/queueing around 16k+ and confirm whether the morning rollout changed the backend kernel config for the hosted cluster serving Novamed. Prioritize rollback if a kernel change is implicated.

Marissa: loop in CS + account team if we need mitigation credits or immediate customer comms. Laura: I'm flagging for visibility. I'll forward findings once we have root cause or mitigation.

Diego Fernandez
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, infra-oncall@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Production alert: p99 latency spikes on long-window requests

Initial triage notes (10:05):
- Observed sustained p99 jump from ~650ms to ~2.6s for sequences >16k tokens across the hosted fleet in us-west-2.
- Throughput (aggregate QPS) for long-window endpoints remained steady; this looks like head-of-line scheduling + kernel codepath latency for long KV-cache loads.
- The morning rollout included a new attention kernel optimization for GPT-like architectures; fallback policy didn't trigger for >32k path as expected.

Immediate actions taken:
- Temporarily pinned Novamed traffic to the previous kernel variant (rolled back the kernel flag for their tenant) at 10:12 PT.
- Enabled aggressive prefix caching for the tenant to reduce KV fetches for repeated prompts.

Preliminary result: p99 dropped to ~780ms within 6 minutes for the pinned nodes, but some traffic still routed to mixed-capacity pools while autoscaler rebalanced.

Next steps:
1) Schedule an urgent canary rollback for the new kernel across the rest of the hosted fleet (if rollback is causal).
2) Generate per-tenant routing report for last 3 hours (INF-3210).
3) Prepare customer-facing incident note with temporary mitigations and ETA.

Marcus Lin
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

-----Forwarded message-----
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Novamed customer update draft / credits

Diego / Laura —
Draft for Novamed (short):

"Novamed team — we detected elevated p99 latency on long-context API calls this morning caused by a runtime kernel change. We've pinned your tenant to the prior kernel, applied prefix caching, and are monitoring; p99 has improved but we are completing a fleet-wide rollback verification. We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a post-mortem and remediation plan."

Can we offer a service credit for the impacted window (08:45–10:30 PT)? Their SLA language gives us room for a partial credit; recommend 20% for the window and an offer for a technical review with our applied-ML team.

Attachments: novamed_kpi_snapshot.pdf

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Customers
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

-----Original Message Continued-----
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, ceo@redwood.ai, head_ops@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec brief: Novamed incident and recommended customer remediation

Team —
Summary (for execs):
- Impact: Novamed reported increased p99 latency affecting clinical workloads using 16k/32k windows (08:45–10:30 PT). Root cause appears to be a kernel optimization rollout that did not fallback cleanly for high-KV paths.
- Customer impact: transient stalls and intermittent 504s; no data loss reported but trial runs slowed.
- Mitigation: tenant pinned to prior kernel, prefix caching applied, fleet rollback in progress. Immediate p99 improved to ~780ms for pinned nodes.
- Business ask: approve a 20% service credit for the affected window and authorize a prioritized technical review (applied ML + runtime) to create a long-window resilience plan.

Action items assigned:
- Marcus: complete rollback verification and provide postmortem notes (INF-3210).
- Marissa: confirm credit amount and prepare customer comms.
- Diego: lead the post-incident technical review with Novamed and schedule a walkthrough.

I'd like sign-off from CEO / Head Ops for the credit and prioritized review. Please reply by EOD if you don't approve.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success and Partnerships
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Exec brief: Novamed incident and recommended customer remediation

Marissa, send the customer note with the language above; include offer for a joint post-mortem next week (we'll include runtime and applied ML engineers).

Priya / Mike — we apologize for the disruption. Expect a written incident note within 24 hours and an invite for a technical walkthrough early next week. We'll also share mitigation engineering work and timeline.

Diego Fernandez
